```{r setup}
library(controlcompR)
```

## The linear quadratic regulator

For \(\dot x = Ax + Bu\), the law \(u = -Kx\) with
\(K = R^{-1}(B^\top P + N^\top)\), where \(P\) is the stabilizing solution
of the continuous algebraic Riccati equation, minimizes
\[
J = \int_0^\infty x^\top Q x + u^\top R u + 2 x^\top N u \, dt .
\]
The conditions are checked: \(R \succ 0\), the joint weight
\(\begin{pmatrix} Q & N \\ N^\top & R\end{pmatrix} \succeq 0\),
\((A, B)\) stabilizable, and no unobservable modes of the cost on the
imaginary axis. The minimum is over stabilizing inputs; it is the
unrestricted minimum when the cost detects every unstable mode. The
optimality statement holds only for this linear model
and this cost; it says nothing about constraints, model error or
nonlinear plants.

```{r}
plant <- ctrl_ss(matrix(c(0, 1, 0, 0), 2, byrow = TRUE), c(0, 1), c(1, 0),
                 state_names = c("position", "velocity"))
lqr <- ctrl_lqr(plant, Q = diag(c(1, 0.1)), R = 0.01)
lqr
```

The returned cost matrix gives the optimal cost from any initial state,
\(J^\star = x_0^\top P x_0\):

```{r}
x0 <- c(1, 0)
drop(t(x0) %*% lqr$P %*% x0)
```

### The weights trade speed against effort

```{r}
designs <- lapply(c(1, 0.1, 0.01), function(r) ctrl_lqr(plant, diag(c(1, 0.1)), r))
sapply(designs, function(d) c(K = d$K, slowest_pole = max(Re(d$poles))))
```

### Closed-loop simulation

```{r}
cl <- ctrl_closed_loop(plant, lqr)
plot(ctrl_initial(cl, x0 = c(1, 0)))
```

The closed loop has the plant outputs followed by the control signals, so
the actuator effort is always visible.

## Discrete and finite-horizon LQR

For discrete models `ctrl_lqr()` solves the discrete Riccati equation.
`ctrl_dlqr_finite()` computes the time-varying gains of the finite-horizon
problem by the backward Riccati recursion; for long horizons the first
gain converges to the infinite-horizon gain:

```{r}
pd <- ctrl_c2d(plant, 0.1)
inf <- ctrl_lqr(pd, diag(c(1, 0.1)), 0.01)
fin <- ctrl_dlqr_finite(pd, diag(c(1, 0.1)), 0.01, horizon = 200)
rbind(infinite = drop(inf$K), finite_first = drop(fin$K[[1]]))
```

## Reference tracking

State feedback regulates to zero. To track a constant reference \(r\),
use \(u = N r - K x\) with the static prefilter `N` that gives unit DC
gain (it exists when the plant has no zero at the origin):

```{r}
N <- ctrl_reference_gain(plant, lqr)
N
plot(ctrl_step(ctrl_series(ctrl_gain(N), cl)))
```

A prefilter is not robust to model error: a constant disturbance or a gain
mismatch leaves a steady-state offset. Integral action (augmenting the
state with the integral of the error) or offset-free MPC removes it.

```{r}
# integral augmentation: z' = r - y
Aa <- rbind(cbind(plant$A, 0), cbind(-plant$C, 0))
Ba <- rbind(plant$B, 0)
aug <- ctrl_ss(Aa, Ba, diag(3))
Ki <- ctrl_lqr(aug, diag(c(1, 0.1, 5)), 0.01)$K
Ki
```

## Pole placement

`ctrl_place()` computes `K` so that \(A - BK\) has prescribed eigenvalues,
with the robust eigenstructure assignment of Kautsky, Nichols and Van
Dooren. For several inputs the remaining freedom is used to make the
closed-loop eigenvectors as well conditioned as possible, and the
condition number is reported because it measures how fragile the
placement is:

```{r}
K <- ctrl_place(plant, poles = c(-2 + 1i, -2 - 1i))
K
eigen(plant$A - plant$B %*% K)$values
attr(K, "cond_X")

A3 <- matrix(c(0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, -2, -3), 3, byrow = TRUE)
B3 <- matrix(c(0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1), 3)
K3 <- ctrl_place(A3, B3, c(-1, -2, -3))
attr(K3, "cond_X")
```

Placing poles far to the left needs large gains, which amplify noise and
saturate actuators. LQR often gives better compromises because the
weights speak directly about states and inputs.
